correctness.rationale: For every n>=4, hub-triangle supports have min0/max2 and full-rim support min0/max n-1. Summing reflected inequalities gives 2n <= s(n-1). At s=2n/(n-1), z=(s+1)c has spoke weight (n+1)/(n-1), rim weight2. For any spanning tree T, y=(z-1_T)/s has y>=0, edge total n, and every Edmonds induced-subgraph inequality: without hub, rim edges <=k-1 (or n if all rim); with hub, selected rim vertices decompose into runs with q components and L isolated interior vertices, forcing T(E(S))>=L and k<=2q+L. Thus y is in the spanning-tree polytope, giving exact upper bound. Equality in triangles and hub-three-rim supports (min1/max3) yields spoke plus shifted rim sum1, then forces the unique coordinates. Exact integer checker verified 3532 trees and 1390868 inequalities for n=4..8; finite cases are supplementary only. Boundary n=3 is excluded.

value.rationale: A natural, connected, planar infinite graphic-matroid family has two distinct edge orbits, mixed clique/cycle constraints, and no immediate reduction to complete or bipartite graph classes. Exact asymmetry and a unique optimal center are determined uniformly, with a new conceptual upper-bound certificate obtained from path-run decomposition and a rigidity argument. The limit of asymmetry is 2 rather than the growing polytope dimension; this yields a meaningful complete geometric classification for the family, not an arbitrary small instance or table lookup.
